```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# SETTING UP LIBRARIES
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(Metrics)
library(forecast)
library(glmnet)
```

## Loading Datasets
```{r}

data = read.csv("../data/data_merged.csv")
data_mean = read.csv("../data/prevail_mean.csv")

data$date <- as.Date(data$date)
data_mean$date <- as.Date(data_mean$date)

# ============================================================================
# CREATE MULTI-HORIZON TARGET VARIABLES
# ============================================================================
# We want to forecast 3-month, 6-month, and 12-month ahead returns
# 6-month = sum of 2 consecutive quarters
# 12-month = sum of 4 consecutive quarters

data <- data %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    # Create lead log returns for each horizon
    log_ret_lead_3m = lead(log_ret, 1),           # 3-month ahead (1 quarter)
    log_ret_lead_6m = lead(log_ret, 1) + lead(log_ret, 2),  # 6-month ahead (2 quarters)
    log_ret_lead_12m = lead(log_ret, 1) + lead(log_ret, 2) + lead(log_ret, 3) + lead(log_ret, 4)  # 12-month ahead (4 quarters)
  )

# ============================================================================
# CREATE LAGGED VARIABLES FOR MULTI-HORIZON TARGETS
# ============================================================================
# Create 5 lags for each horizon's returns

# Lags for 3-month returns
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    log_ret_3m_L1 = lag(log_ret_lead_3m, 1),
    log_ret_3m_L2 = lag(log_ret_lead_3m, 2),
    log_ret_3m_L3 = lag(log_ret_lead_3m, 3),
    log_ret_3m_L4 = lag(log_ret_lead_3m, 4),
    log_ret_3m_L5 = lag(log_ret_lead_3m, 5)
  )

# ============================================================================
# SELECT FINAL FEATURES FOR MODELING
# ============================================================================

data <- data %>%
  select(
    date,
    log_ret,
    # Multi-horizon targets
    log_ret_lead_3m,
    log_ret_lead_6m,
    log_ret_lead_12m,
    # All lagged y's for 3-month horizon
    matches("^log_ret_3m_L"),
    # ALL lagged x variables (L2-L5 only to avoid leakage with 1-quarter lead)
    matches("_L[2-5]$")
  )

cat("\n=== Multi-Horizon Target Variables Created ===\n")
cat("✓ log_ret_lead_3m: 3-month ahead returns (1 quarter)\n")
cat("✓ log_ret_lead_6m: 6-month ahead returns (sum of 2 quarters)\n")
cat("✓ log_ret_lead_12m: 12-month ahead returns (sum of 4 quarters)\n")
cat("✓ 5 lags created for each horizon\n")

# ============================================================================
# DIAGNOSTIC: Show all available columns with lag variables
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== All Columns in Data ===\n")
all_cols <- colnames(data)
cat("Total columns:", length(all_cols), "\n")
cat("Columns:", paste(all_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")

cat("\n=== Lag Columns (containing _L2, _L3, _L4, or _L5) ===\n")
lag_cols <- grep("_L[2-5]$", all_cols, value = TRUE)
cat("Total lag variables (L2-L5):", length(lag_cols), "\n")
print(lag_cols)

cat("\n=== 3-month Horizon Lag Columns ===\n")
lag_3m <- grep("^log_ret_3m_L", all_cols, value = TRUE)
cat("Total 3m lag variables:", length(lag_3m), "\n")
print(lag_3m)

cat("\n=== FEATURE SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("log_ret_3m_L* (3m horizon lags):", length(lag_3m), "\n")
cat("_L[2-5]$ (all L2-L5 variables):", length(lag_cols), "\n")
cat("TOTAL FEATURES FOR MODELING:", length(lag_3m) + length(lag_cols), "\n")

```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# REMOVE NA VALUES (ONLY LAGGED AND LEAD VARIABLES)
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== Removing NA Values ===\n")
cat("Observations before drop_na():", nrow(data), "\n")

# Remove all rows with any NA values
data_clean <- data %>%
  drop_na()

cat("Observations after drop_na():", nrow(data_clean), "\n")
cat("Rows removed:", nrow(data) - nrow(data_clean), "\n\n")

# Show date range of clean data

```

# ============================================================================
# MODELING APPROACH: 80/20 Train-Test Split w/ Recursive CV
# ============================================================================

```{r}
# --- STEP 1: Prepare data ---

elastic_net_df <- data_clean %>%
  arrange(date)

set.seed(123)

n <- nrow(elastic_net_df)
train_size <- floor(0.8 * n)  # 80% training
test_size <- n - train_size   # 20% testing

cat("\n=== Data Split ===\n")
cat("Total observations:", n, "\n")
cat("Training:", train_size, "observations\n")
cat("Testing :", test_size, "observations\n")

train_data <- elastic_net_df[1:train_size, ]
test_data  <- elastic_net_df[(train_size + 1):n, ]

# ============================================================================
# PREPARE DATA FOR MULTI-HORIZON FORECASTING
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== Multi-Horizon Models Setup ===\n")

# Define horizons
horizons <- c("3m", "6m", "12m")

# Get COMMON features used for ALL horizons
# (only log_ret_3m_L1-L5 lag variables + all L2-L5 economic indicators)
common_features <- elastic_net_df %>%
  select(
    matches("^log_ret_3m_L"),   # log_ret_3m_L1-L5
    matches("_L[2-5]$")          # ALL L2-L5 variables (including log_ret_3m_L2-L5 which overlap)
  ) %>%
  names() %>%
  unique()

cat("\nCommon features for ALL horizons:\n")
cat("  Total features:", length(common_features), "\n")
cat("  Feature names:", paste(common_features, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# For each horizon, prepare X and y with the SAME features
for (horizon in horizons) {
  
  # Select the target variable for this horizon
  target_col <- paste0("log_ret_lead_", horizon)
  
  # All three horizons use the SAME feature set
  feature_cols <- common_features
  
  # Training set
  X_train_temp <- train_data %>%
    select(all_of(feature_cols)) %>%
    as.matrix()
  
  y_train_temp <- train_data[[target_col]]
  
  # Test set
  X_test_temp <- test_data %>%
    select(all_of(feature_cols)) %>%
    as.matrix()
  
  y_test_temp <- test_data[[target_col]]
  
  # Assign to environment with horizon-specific names
  assign(paste0("X_train_", horizon), X_train_temp)
  assign(paste0("y_train_", horizon), y_train_temp)
  assign(paste0("X_test_", horizon), X_test_temp)
  assign(paste0("y_test_", horizon), y_test_temp)
  
  cat("\nHorizon:", horizon, "\n")
  cat("  Features:", ncol(X_train_temp), "\n")
  cat("  Train observations:", nrow(X_train_temp), "\n")
  cat("  Test observations:", nrow(X_test_temp), "\n")
}

```

## Helper Functions: BIC-based Lambda Selection

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# BIC-based Lambda Selection Functions (Kock & Callot)
# BIC(λ) = log(RSS(λ)) + (log(T)/T)·df(λ)
# ============================================================================

# Function 1: Compute degrees of freedom for Elastic Net
# For Elastic Net: df(λ) ≈ number of non-zero coefficients (excluding intercept)
compute_elastic_net_df <- function(fit_object, lambda) {
  # Get coefficients at this lambda
  coefs <- coef(fit_object, s = lambda)
  # df = number of non-zero coefficients (excluding intercept)
  df <- sum(coefs[-1] != 0)
  return(df)
}

# Function 2: Fit Elastic Net Regression and compute BIC for each lambda
fit_elastic_net_bic <- function(X, y, alpha = 0.5, lambdas = NULL) {
  
  # ---- Input validation ----
  T <- nrow(X)
  
  if (length(y) != T) stop("X and y must have same number of rows")
  if (!is.matrix(X)) X <- as.matrix(X)
  
  # Fit glmnet (Elastic Net: alpha=0.5, standardize=TRUE, intercept=TRUE)
  fit <- glmnet(X, y, alpha = alpha, standardize = TRUE, intercept = TRUE, 
                lambda = lambdas, thresh = 1e-7)
  
  # ---- Compute RSS on training data ----
  # Get predictions for each lambda
  y_pred_matrix <- predict(fit, newx = X, s = fit$lambda)
  
  # RSS for each lambda
  RSS_vec <- colSums((y - y_pred_matrix)^2)
  
  # ---- Compute degrees of freedom for each lambda ----
  df_vec <- sapply(fit$lambda, function(lam) {
    compute_elastic_net_df(fit, lam)
  })
  
  # ---- Compute BIC: log(RSS) + (log(T)/T) * df ----
  bic_penalty <- log(T) / T
  BIC_vec <- log(RSS_vec) + bic_penalty * df_vec
  
  # ---- Find optimal lambda ----
  idx_best <- which.min(BIC_vec)
  lambda_best <- fit$lambda[idx_best]
  
  # ---- Create results table ----
  bic_tbl <- data.frame(
    lambda = fit$lambda,
    RSS = RSS_vec,
    df = df_vec,
    BIC = BIC_vec,
    is_best = (fit$lambda == lambda_best)
  )
  
  # ---- Return results ----
  return(list(
    lambda_best = lambda_best,
    bic_tbl = bic_tbl,
    fit = fit
  ))
}

# Function 3: Helper to select lambda by BIC
# Dispatches based on alpha (0=Ridge, 0.5=Elastic Net, 1=Lasso)
select_lambda_bic <- function(X, y, alpha = 0.5, lambdas = NULL) {
  
  if (is.null(lambdas)) {
    # Generate default lambda sequence (glmnet default behavior)
    lambdas <- 10^seq(5, -2, length.out = 100)
  }
  
  if (alpha == 0.5) {
    # Elastic Net (combination of Ridge and Lasso)
    result <- fit_elastic_net_bic(X, y, alpha = 0.5, lambdas = lambdas)
  } else if (alpha == 0) {
    # Ridge (not used here)
    stop("Use alpha=0.5 for Elastic Net. For Ridge, use ridge_regression.Rmd")
  } else if (alpha == 1) {
    # Lasso (not used here)
    stop("Use alpha=0.5 for Elastic Net. For Lasso, use lasso_regression.Rmd")
  } else {
    stop("alpha must be 0.5 (Elastic Net)")
  }
  
  return(result)
}

```

## Build Elastic Net Models for Each Horizon

```{r}
# ---- Fit Elastic Net Regression Models for Each Horizon (3m, 6m, 12m) ----
# Each horizon gets its own independent BIC optimization

# Lambda sequence for BIC optimization
lambdas <- 10^seq(3, -1, length.out = 50)

# Store results for each horizon
elastic_net_results <- list()

# Loop through each horizon
for (horizon in c("3m", "6m", "12m")) {
  cat("\n========== HORIZON:", horizon, "==========\n")
  
  # Extract datasets for this horizon (horizon-specific features only)
  X_train_h <- get(paste0("X_train_", horizon))
  y_train_h <- get(paste0("y_train_", horizon))
  X_test_h <- get(paste0("X_test_", horizon))
  y_test_h <- get(paste0("y_test_", horizon))
  
  cat("Features for", horizon, "horizon:", ncol(X_train_h), "variables\n")
  cat("Sample features:", paste(colnames(X_train_h)[seq_len(min(3, ncol(X_train_h)))], collapse = ", "), "\n")
  
  # Fit Elastic Net regression with BIC lambda selection
  # BIC optimization is done INDEPENDENTLY for each horizon
  elastic_net_fit <- select_lambda_bic(X_train_h, y_train_h, 
                                       alpha = 0.5, 
                                       lambdas = lambdas)
  
  # Store the result
  elastic_net_results[[horizon]] <- elastic_net_fit
  
  # Extract optimal lambda and model
  lambda_opt <- elastic_net_fit$lambda_best
  fit_glmnet <- elastic_net_fit$fit
  
  cat("\nOptimal lambda (BIC) for", horizon, ":", lambda_opt, "\n")
  cat("Top 10 BIC values:\n")
  print(head(elastic_net_fit$bic_tbl, 10))
  
  # Make predictions on test set
  y_pred_test <- as.vector(predict(fit_glmnet, newx = X_test_h, s = lambda_opt))
  
  # Make predictions on training set
  y_pred_train <- as.vector(predict(fit_glmnet, newx = X_train_h, s = lambda_opt))
  
  # Compute test metrics (RMSE = sqrt(mean(squared errors)))
  rmse_test <- sqrt(mean((y_test_h - y_pred_test)^2))
  
  # Compute training metrics
  rmse_train <- sqrt(mean((y_train_h - y_pred_train)^2))
  
  # Display metrics
  cat("\nTest Set Metrics:\n")
  cat("  RMSE:", rmse_test, "\n")
  
  cat("\nTraining Set Metrics:\n")
  cat("  RMSE:", rmse_train, "\n")
  
  # Extract coefficients
  coefficients <- as.vector(coef(fit_glmnet, s = lambda_opt))
  
  # Create results dataframe for test predictions
  test_results <- data.frame(
    actual = y_test_h,
    predicted = y_pred_test,
    residual = y_test_h - y_pred_test,
    abs_error = abs(y_test_h - y_pred_test)
  )
  
  # Create results dataframe for training predictions
  train_results <- data.frame(
    actual = y_train_h,
    predicted = y_pred_train,
    residual = y_train_h - y_pred_train,
    abs_error = abs(y_train_h - y_pred_train)
  )
  
  # Create metrics summary
  metrics_summary <- data.frame(
    Horizon = horizon,
    Dataset = c("Training", "Test"),
    RMSE = c(rmse_train, rmse_test),
    Lambda_Optimal = lambda_opt,
    N_NonZero_Coefs = sum(coefficients[-1] != 0)  # Exclude intercept
  )
  
  # Store results and metrics in lists for later visualization
  elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$train_results <- train_results
  elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$test_results <- test_results
  elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$metrics_summary <- metrics_summary
  elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$train_data_dates <- train_data$date
  elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$test_data_dates <- test_data$date
  
  cat("\n")
}

cat("\n========== ELASTIC NET REGRESSION MODELS COMPLETE ==========\n")

# Create cross-horizon summary
cat("\nCross-Horizon Summary:\n")
summary_list <- lapply(c("3m", "6m", "12m"), function(horizon) {
  elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$metrics_summary
})
summary_table <- do.call(rbind, summary_list)
print(summary_table)

```

## Visualizations: Elastic Net Regression Results for Each Horizon

```{r}
# ---- Visualize Test Set: Forecasted vs Actual for Each Horizon ----

for (horizon in c("3m", "6m", "12m")) {
  
  test_results <- elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$test_results
  test_dates <- elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$test_data_dates
  
  # Add dates to results
  test_results$date <- test_dates
  
  metrics <- elastic_net_results[[horizon]]$metrics_summary
  test_metrics <- metrics[metrics$Dataset == "Test", ]
  
  # Line plot: Forecasted vs Actual for test set
  p <- ggplot(test_results, aes(x = date)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = actual, color = "Actual"), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_line(aes(y = predicted, color = "Elastic Net Forecast"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Elastic Net Regression:", toupper(horizon), "Horizon - Test Set"),
      x = "Date",
      y = "Log Return",
      color = "Series",
      subtitle = paste("RMSE =", round(test_metrics$RMSE, 4))
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual" = "steelblue", "Elastic Net Forecast" = "coral")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  print(p)
}

```

```{r}
# ---- Visualize training set: Forecasted vs Actual ----

# Create a data frame for training set plotting
train_results <- data.frame(
  date = train_data$date,
  actual = y_train,
  forecasted = as.numeric(y_pred_train),
  obs_num = seq_along(y_train)
)

# Line plot: Forecasted vs Actual for training set
ggplot(train_results, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = actual, color = "Actual"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = forecasted, color = "Elastic Net Forecast"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Elastic Net Regression: Forecasted vs Actual Returns (Training Set)",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Log Return",
    color = "Series"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual" = "steelblue", "Elastic Net Forecast" = "coral")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```

```{r}
# ---- Scatter plot: Training set Forecasted vs Actual ----

# Compute training metrics for display
mae_train <- mae(y_train, y_pred_train)
rmse_train <- rmse(y_train, y_pred_train)
r2_train <- cor(y_train, y_pred_train)^2

ggplot(train_results, aes(x = actual, y = forecasted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Elastic Net Regression: Training Set Forecast Accuracy",
    x = "Actual Return",
    y = "Forecasted Return",
    subtitle = paste("R² =", round(r2_train, 4), "| RMSE =", round(rmse_train, 6))
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1)

```
